finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /restore passes attacker-supplied base64 to Marshal.load, which can instantiate arbitrary classes and invoke their marshal hooks. This is a code-execution primitive; practical RCE depends on a gadget class in the loaded gem set, which I did not verify with a working payload.

trace.note: post "/restore" route accepts unauthenticated POST requests
params[:state] read from request, passed through Base64.decode64 (lenient decoder)
decoded bytes passed directly to Marshal.load
state.inspect returns the deserialized object's representation to the client

finding.guards_checked: None. No authentication, no HMAC/signature over the state blob, no class allowlist, no size limit, no type check before or after load. Secondary: state.inspect output is served as text/html (Sinatra default) and String#inspect does not escape < or >, so a crafted string can also yield reflected XSS.

verdict.guard_found: none. app.rb:5 declares the POST /restore route with no auth, app.rb:6 passes params[:state] through Base64.decode64 straight into Marshal.load with no signature, allowlist, or size check, and app.rb:7 returns state.inspect. The directory holds only app.rb, with no Gemfile, middleware, or config that could add a guard.
verdict.reason: The POST /restore route at app.rb:5-6 is reachable anonymously and feeds attacker-controlled base64 into Marshal.load with no guard, which is an unsafe-deserialization sink (CWE-502). Whether a working RCE gadget exists depends on the loaded gems, which I did not verify; the reflected-XSS side claim via state.inspect at app.rb:7 is also plausible under Sinatra's default text/html but I did not test it.

finding.claim: Unauthenticated POST /import reflects attacker-chosen JSON object key names unescaped into the response body, which Sinatra serves as text/html, enabling reflected HTML/XSS injection via a cross-site auto-submitting form.
finding.source: Request body read at app.rb:11 (request.body.read), parsed by JSON.parse; key names are attacker-controlled
finding.sink: Response body from data.keys.join(",") at app.rb:12

trace.note: post "/import" route accepts unauthenticated POST requests; no explicit Content-Type set
request.body.read parsed with JSON.parse into attacker-controlled hash
data.keys joined with commas and returned as response body without escaping

finding.guards_checked: No HTML escaping, no explicit Content-Type override to text/plain or application/json, no CSRF protection, no origin/Referer check. Low-severity related issue: non-object JSON (array/scalar) raises NoMethodError at app.rb:12 (500), and malformed JSON raises JSON::ParserError at app.rb:11; these are availability/error-disclosure concerns, not standalone security boundaries.

verdict.guard_found: Sinatra's default Rack::Protection middleware (HttpOrigin and RemoteToken, enabled by default in classic Sinatra apps). app.rb sets no `protection` override, so it is active. Its installed source is not in the directory, so this rests on the framework default and not on code I could read.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (app.rb:10-12: the POST /import route reads the body, parses it with JSON.parse, and returns data.keys.join(",") unescaped), and the attacker is anonymous. But a cross-site auto-submitting form POST carries an Origin header and no matching Referer, which Sinatra's default Rack::Protection HttpOrigin/RemoteToken checks reject before the route runs, and app.rb:5-17 does not disable them. The candidate's claim that there is "no origin/Referer check" is therefore wrong, unless the app runs with protection disabled, which I cannot see in the repo.
